tagline: Across the west desert on the mail riders' line.
intro: The byway turns off SR-73 near Fairfield and heads west on maintained gravel across Utah's west desert, over bare desert ranges and across wide basins, on the line the Pony Express riders took in 1860 and 1861. Every ten miles or so the remains of an old station sit beside the road. It ends in Goshute country at Ibapah, near the Nevada line.

The riders carried the nation's priority mail from Missouri to California in as little as ten days. The service lasted only until the transcontinental telegraph was finished, and it never made a profit.

moments.title: Fairfield
moments.text: When Johnston's Army camped nearby in 1858 and 1859, the place then called Frogtown swelled past 7,000 people, and its Stagecoach Inn took in soldiers, stage travelers and Pony Express riders.

moments.title: Simpson Springs
moments.text: A long-relied-on water source on the trail west, it served the mule mail, the Pony Express and the Overland Stage, and the station building there now is a 1975 replica.

moments.title: Fish Springs
moments.text: The road runs through a refuge of warm, salty springs whose fish, reported at over six inches long, are left over from ancient Lake Bonneville.

practical: The byway is a maintained gravel road.
